# Topic: Ethiopia & East Africa
injera|A large, soft, slightly sour flatbread made from fermented teff batter; the base of most Ethiopian meals.|እንጀራ|injeera|እንጀራ|canjeero|إنجيرا
teff|A tiny, nutritious grain native to Ethiopia, ground into flour to make injera.|ጤፍ|xaafii|||
berbere|A fiery Ethiopian spice blend of dried chili, garlic, ginger and aromatic seeds.|በርበሬ|||በርበረ|
shiro|A thick stew of ground chickpea or broad-bean flour simmered with onion, garlic and berbere.|ሽሮ|shiroo|ሽሮ||
doro wat|A spicy chicken stew with hard-boiled eggs, served at feasts and holidays.|ዶሮ ወጥ|doro wat|ጸብሒ ደርሆ||
kitfo|Minced beef seasoned with mitmita and spiced butter, eaten raw, lightly cooked or well done.|ክትፎ|kitfoo|ክትፎ||
tej|A traditional Ethiopian honey wine, flavoured with the leaves of gesho.|ጠጅ|daadhii|ጠጅ||
coffee ceremony|A traditional ritual in which green coffee is roasted, ground, brewed and served in three rounds.|የቡና ሥነ ሥርዓት|sirna bunaa|ስነ ስርዓት ቡን||
jebena|A round-bottomed clay pot with a long neck, used to brew coffee in Ethiopia and Eritrea.|ጀበና|jabanaa|ጀበና||
birr|The currency of Ethiopia.|ብር|birrii|ብር|birr|بير
Merkato|One of the largest open-air markets in Africa, in the heart of Addis Ababa.|መርካቶ|Merkaatoo|መርካቶ||
Meskel|An Ethiopian Orthodox festival on 27 September marking the finding of the True Cross, with a bonfire (demera).|መስቀል|Masqala|መስቀል||
Timkat|The Ethiopian Orthodox celebration of Epiphany on 19 January, with processions and blessing of water.|ጥምቀት||ጥምቀት||
Enkutatash|The Ethiopian New Year, celebrated on 11 September (12 in a leap year) at the end of the rainy season.|እንቁጣጣሽ|Bara haaraa|ሓድሽ ዓመት||
Irreecha|The Oromo thanksgiving festival, held by lakes and rivers after the rainy season.|ኢሬቻ|Irreecha|||
Gada system|The traditional democratic system of the Oromo people, in which leadership passes between age-grade groups every eight years.|ገዳ ሥርዓት|sirna Gadaa|||
Ethiopian calendar|A calendar of thirteen months, twelve of thirty days and one of five or six, about seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar.|የኢትዮጵያ ዘመን አቆጣጠር||||
Ge'ez|An ancient Semitic language, still the liturgical language of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church, and the name of the script used to write Amharic and Tigrinya.|ግዕዝ|Gi'iiz|ግዕዝ||
fidel|The Ethiopic script (Ge'ez script), an abugida in which each symbol stands for a consonant and a vowel.|ፊደል||ፊደል||
Lalibela|A town in northern Ethiopia famous for eleven medieval rock-hewn churches, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.|ላሊበላ|Laalibalaa|ላሊበላ||
Axum|An ancient city in northern Ethiopia, once the capital of the Aksumite Empire, known for its giant stone obelisks.|አክሱም|Aksum|ኣኽሱም||
Blue Nile|The river that flows from Lake Tana and joins the White Nile at Khartoum; called Abay in Ethiopia.|ዓባይ|Abbaay|ዓባይ||
Lake Tana|The largest lake in Ethiopia, source of the Blue Nile, dotted with ancient island monasteries.|ጣና ሐይቅ|Haroo Taanaa|||
Simien Mountains|A mountain range with dramatic cliffs in northern Ethiopia, home of the gelada baboon and walia ibex.|ስሚን ተራሮች||||
Great Rift Valley|A vast geological trench running through East Africa, with lakes, volcanoes and hot springs.|ታላቁ ስምጥ ሸለቆ||||
Harar|A walled historic city in eastern Ethiopia, an important centre of Islamic learning and trade.|ሐረር|Hararee|ሐረር||
Finfinnee|The Oromo name of Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia.|ፊንፊኔ|Finfinnee|||
Afaan Oromo|The Cushitic language of the Oromo people, one of the most widely spoken languages in Africa.|ኦሮምኛ|Afaan Oromoo|ኦሮምኛ||
Tigrinya|A Semitic language spoken in Tigray (Ethiopia) and Eritrea, written in the Ge'ez script.|ትግርኛ|Tigiriffa|ትግርኛ||
Somali language|The Cushitic language of the Somali people, spoken in Somalia, Ethiopia, Djibouti and Kenya.|ሶማልኛ|Afaan Somaalee||Af-Soomaali|اللغة الصومالية
gursha|An Ethiopian custom of feeding someone a mouthful of food by hand as a sign of friendship and respect.|ጉርሻ||||
mesob|A woven, basket-like table at which injera and stews are served and shared.|መሶብ||||
netela|A thin white cotton shawl with a coloured woven border, worn traditionally in Ethiopia.|ነጠላ||||
habesha kemis|The traditional white cotton dress of Ethiopian women, with woven or embroidered borders.|ሀበሻ ቀሚስ||||
